user.title: Alpha EMS Manager
user.description: Alpha EMS Manager learns how much electricity your household actually uses. It reads entities that other integrations already provide and never contacts an external service itself.

data_description.name: Used for the device name and the entity ids. Leave it as Alpha EMS unless you run more than one instance.
data_description.house_load_entity: Instantaneous household consumption in W or kW, independent of solar, battery and grid flows. On AlphaESS this is Current House Load.
data_description.daily_house_load_entity: Optional cumulative daily total in kWh, used only as an end-of-day cross-check. It is never used as the learning source.
data_description.has_pv: Enables the solar production source on the next screens.
data_description.use_pv_forecast: Requires a configured Solcast PV Forecast integration. When on, expected production is netted against predicted load and recorded as evidence against what the panels actually produced.
data_description.ev_power_entity: Optional. If your EV charges behind the house-load meter, select its power sensor here and Alpha EMS will learn household demand with EV charging removed. Any W or kW sensor works; no particular charger brand is assumed.

battery.title: Battery
battery.description: Select the battery sensors, confirm how your system reports charging, and enter the battery's own limits. The limits are used only to work out what the battery could do; Alpha EMS never sends a command to it.

data_description.battery_soc_entity: A percentage sensor, for example AlphaESS SoC Battery.
data_description.battery_power_entity: Instantaneous battery power in W or kW.
data_description.battery_power_sign: Check a moment when the battery is charging. AlphaESS reports a negative value while charging, which is the default here.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: The usable energy of the pack itself, on the DC side, in kWh. Take the usable figure from your battery's data sheet rather than a charge or discharge test result, which is measured on the AC side and is a few per cent smaller. Nothing can work this out from a percentage sensor, so it has no default: leave it empty and the battery planning stays unavailable rather than guessing.
data_description.battery_min_soc_percent: The lowest state of charge the planning will ever use. It is a hard floor: no recommendation and no simulation crosses it. 0 % is allowed and means no reserve of its own, in which case only your inverter's own floor applies.
data_description.battery_max_charge_kw: The most the battery can be charged at, measured on the AC side, in kW. Usually the inverter's rating. No default, for the same reason as capacity.
data_description.battery_max_discharge_kw: The most the battery can be discharged at, measured on the AC side, in kW. Usually the inverter's rating.
data_description.battery_round_trip_efficiency_percent: How much of the energy put in comes back out again, AC to AC, as a percentage. Around 90 % is typical for a home battery. Enter 90, not 0.9.

solar.title: Solar production
solar.description: Select the sensor that reports how much your panels are generating right now.

data_description.pv_power_entity: Instantaneous solar generation in W or kW. Recorded per quarter-hour for the energy-balance check and as evidence against the forecast; it never changes the learned household load.

grid.title: Grid meter
grid.description: Any meter integration works here, such as HomeWizard P1, DSMR or SlimmeLezer.

data_description.grid_power_entity: Instantaneous grid exchange in W or kW.
data_description.grid_power_sign: Check a moment when you are drawing from the grid. Most Dutch meters report a positive value while importing, which is the default here.

sources.title: Prices and forecast
sources.description: Alpha EMS Manager reads these integrations through Home Assistant. It never calls their APIs and never duplicates their entities.

data_description.frank_entry_id: Selecting the integration instead of individual entities means renaming an entity later will not break anything.
data_description.solcast_entry_id: Only required because you enabled the PV forecast.

control.title: Control
control.description: How Alpha EMS should behave if it is ever allowed to act on its own recommendation. This release cannot send a command to your inverter at all: the control pipeline is built and checked end to end, and the final step that would write to the battery is unavailable. Set the Control Mode entity to Shadow to watch what it would have done.

data_description.control_horizon_minutes: How long a command would tell the inverter to hold, in minutes. This is a safety timeout rather than a delivery time: the plan is rebuilt every fifteen minutes and each command replaces the last, so it only matters if Alpha EMS stops running -- then the inverter returns to normal by itself once this expires. It has to be longer than fifteen minutes or a command would lapse before the next one arrived.
data_description.control_export_margin_percent: How far below your current house load a discharge command must stay, in percent. A forced discharge sets the battery's rate, so anything the house cannot use goes out to the grid -- and the inverter's own feed-in limit does not apply to it. If a command would exceed this, the whole command is refused rather than made smaller.

economics.title: Economics
economics.description: What Alpha EMS should consider worth doing with your battery. These settings change the plan it publishes and the figures beside it -- they do not make anything happen. This release sends no command to your inverter, so an economic plan here is a recommendation you can watch, compare against your bill and disagree with.

data_description.minimum_trade_gain_eur: How much a single charge or discharge has to earn before it is worth planning, in euros. Charged once per stretch of one action, not per kilowatt-hour, which is what stops a plan full of two-cent trades that wear the battery for nothing. Zero means take every trade the prices justify. This is not a wear model: it is your answer to "how small is too small". Charging to protect the reserve ignores it, because keeping the house supplied is not a trade -- and so does your own solar entering the battery, because nobody chose to do that.
data_description.grid_charge_margin_eur_per_kwh: An additional economic requirement, in euros per kilowatt-hour, on the energy a charge actually causes to be bought from the grid. Zero -- the default -- behaves exactly as before, so upgrading changes nothing until you set it. It exists because the minimum gain per trade is a fixed amount: once a trade clears it the volume behind it is unconstrained, so a fourteen-kilowatt-hour round trip can be planned while earning under four cents a kilowatt-hour. Set this and every bought kilowatt-hour has to earn its keep, not just the trade as a whole. Four things are outside it by construction: your own solar entering the battery, the solar share of a quarter that mixes sun and grid, discharging to supply the house, and charging to protect the reserve -- keeping the house supplied outranks every economic figure. It is not a wear model.
data_description.allow_grid_charging: Whether the plan may **buy** energy from the grid to put in the battery. Off by default, because a battery that only ever stores your own solar cannot lose money on a price forecast. Turning it on lets the plan buy in cheap hours -- and lets it plan a safety purchase when the reserve cannot be met from your panels. This is about buying only: your panels filling the battery is not grid charging, needs no permission, and shows as "hold" rather than "charge".
data_description.allow_battery_export: Whether the plan may sell stored energy back to the grid. Off by default. Turning it on lets the plan value your battery at the export price rather than only at the import price it avoids, which usually finds more to do in the evening peak. Note that no inverter command for this exists in this release, so the plan will show it as wanted and unavailable -- which is the point: you can see what it is worth before anything is built to do it.

options.positive_is_import: Positive means importing from the grid
options.negative_is_import: Negative means importing from the grid
